podcast.title: Drums on "Dream Weaver" (Gary Wright)
podcast.body: The human drums featured on Gary Wright's song "Dream Weaver" were played by Art Wood, distinguishing them from the pure synthesizer elements found elsewhere on the record. "The else on that record is pure synthesizer, but the drums, that's a human, Art Wood."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the Drum Machine

podcast.title: Studio Drummer for Linn LM-1 Samples
podcast.body: Art Wood, a studio drummer who had played with notable artists like Tina Turner, James Brown, and Bette Midler, was hired by Roger Linn to provide the real drum samples for the Linn LM-1 drum computer. He recorded these samples by repeatedly hitting his drum kit while isolated in a closet at Linn's house. "He brought in a studio drummer named Art Wood."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the Drum Machine

podcast.title: Ubiquitous Sampled Sound
podcast.body: Through his samples being used in the Linn LM-1 and subsequent LinnDrum, Art Wood technically appeared on thousands of recordings, often without physically playing, as demonstrated by his presence in recordings by artists like The Human League. "So technically, Art Wood has appeared on thousands of recordings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the Drum Machine

xref.title: Art Wood's "Invisible" Performance
xref.body: The sampled drums by Art Wood, derived from the Linn LM-1 and LinnDrum, were featured in The Human League's music, illustrating how his drumming sound could be present on recordings without his physical presence in the band. "Here, for example, this is Art playing with the human league, without actually having to play with the human league."

xref.title: Collaboration with Steve Porcaro and Art Wood
xref.body: Following suggestions from Steve Porcaro, the keyboardist of Toto, Linn enlisted studio drummer Art Wood to record drum samples for the LM-1. Wood was placed in a closet at Linn's house and tasked with repeatedly hitting various parts of his drum kit. "Following some suggestions by Steve Becaro, the keyboardist in the band Toto, he brought in a studio drummer named Art Wood."
